components.cost_effect: Distribution preprocessing and sampling are additional arithmetic/randomness, not additional SFO calls.
components.goal: Convert a weighted sum of expected squared gradients into an expected guarantee at one output.
components.name: Descent-weighted output
components.operation: Normalize positive w_k=2 gamma_k-L gamma_k^2 and draw an independent output index.
components.requires: 0<gamma_k<2/L; deterministic steps and output draw independent of oracle samples.
transfer_checks: Last-iterate, adaptive output weights or high-probability guarantees require separate arguments.

content.family: Randomized stochastic gradient with descent-weighted random output

limitations.statement: The source's unconditioned A1 wording alone is not used to justify the conditional cancellation (2.10) for general dependent noise.
This is selected Algorithm performance with prescribed randomized output, not a lower bound or a characterization of unrestricted Oracle Complexity.

performance_links.scope_note: Only the selected fresh independent sample conditions and expected squared-gradient output of thm.P035.rsg_bound.

variants.cost: Printed stopped execution uses R SFO calls, at most N, with one vector update per call. Full-trajectory implementation uses N calls. Additional arithmetic: O(N) scalar preprocessing and storage for a cumulative distribution, one scalar random draw and a search to sample R; vector updates cost O(n) arithmetic each and O(n) iterate storage in the stopped implementation. These implementation costs are separately accounted bookkeeping, not source claims of bit complexity. No function-value or exact-gradient evaluation is required.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF pages 5–6, section 2.1 RSG box, (2.2)–(2.3) and following equivalence discussion
variants.name: Fresh independent sample RSG
variants.output: x_R. Equivalently run the full N-step trajectory and select x_R with an independent R of the same distribution.
public_inputs: L>0 and deterministic steps gamma_1,...,gamma_N with 0<gamma_k<2/L
variants.query_and_update: For k=1,...,R, query G(x_k,xi_k), then set x_{k+1}=x_k-gamma_k G(x_k,xi_k), as in (2.2). Output x_R, not x_{R+1}. The final query/update is retained to match the printed algorithm even though it does not affect x_R.
variants.requirements: Euclidean R^n; differentiable globally L-smooth f bounded below. At each query use a fresh independent sample xi_k; for every deterministic x, E G(x,xi_k)=gradient f(x) and E||G(x,xi_k)-gradient f(x)||^2<=sigma^2, uniformly in x,k. Borel measurable oracle. This explicitly selected scope is stronger than the source's wording of A1.
variants.state_and_initialization: Set current iterate to deterministic x1. Define w_k=2 gamma_k-L gamma_k^2 and S=sum_{j=1}^N w_j. Draw R with probability w_k/S, independently of all oracle samples. Retain x_R when reached.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Use p_k=w_k/S from (2.3). Stop after iteration R<=N. This variant takes its steps as public inputs and does not require f*, Delta or sigma for the distribution; it makes no constant-step corollary claim.

use_restrictions: Restricted to fresh independent samples and the specified output distribution. No independent review acceptance or publication is claimed.

links.note: Same-batch selected performance theorem; revisions to be bound by trusted prepare.

summary: Random stopping with descent-weighted output; at most N stochastic gradient calls under the selected independent-sample oracle.
title: RSG: selected fresh independent sample variant
use_when: Seek an expected squared-gradient guarantee with a finite SFO budget; do not substitute last-iterate output.
